action: subtract an oblique half-space normal to the selected base-volume orientation
divergence: Measured on a bare extruded body, uncut by the envelope: massv2 shear removes 140 m3 (subtract) acting on 1 volume(s) (single). The BOOK records this word as subtract on single volumes. The two agree on both counts, so the second implementation is a restatement rather than a different word - it may still differ in proportion, which this bench does not measure.

mathematical_basis.reference: Affine transform: a 4x4 homogeneous matrix, invertible, straight lines preserved
mathematical_basis.definition: The BOOK page reads shear as subtracting an oblique half-space normal to the base-volume orientation, which is a Boolean cut, not the volume-preserving affine shear of the same name. The two senses differ in whether volume survives.
mathematical_basis.shipped_as: 3ds Max Slice (the BOOK sense) vs Skew (the affine sense)

delivery_contract.why: A unary AST chain, a decompose() != 1 refusal inside every macro, and a maximum_components=1 promotion gate. The reason is written in candidate_analysis.py: a detached piece is no more architectural than a small Lego speck, and split wings or arrays must be joined by an explicit bridge or spine.
delivery_contract.note: So the BOOK record's `multiple` means how many volumes the operative involves, NOT how many bodies come back.
